title: Written music costs spontaneity as the Basie band grew
summary: Reading arrangements loses feeling, and the enlarged band turned into an ensemble band with fewer soloists.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You've got to have music. Because you have to have music, see. When you have to rehearse and learn the music, you don't have the freedom that you had when everything was head. Because, you know, you're looking at the music when you're playing. Therefore, you lose a little of your feeling,

you know, playing somebody else's notes, you know. But when you've got your own notes you're playing, you know what you're playing. And you are more at ease playing. But as he added instruments, that's when the band became more musical and more ensembles, you see. And the soloists -- now he has no soloists at all. The band is strictly an ensemble band, you know. And that's one thing I think Basie misses, too, is soloists in his band. Because he's used to having solos like --
